facts.text: Cambridge was platted in November 1856 by Josiah Chandler, who named it after Cambridge, England.
The arrival of the Paul Railroad in 1869 spurred mills, creameries, and farms that still define the town.
Norwegian immigrants began arriving around 1860, establishing Lutheran churches that shaped Cambridge's cultural identity.
The Cambridge Historical Association published "Cambridge, Iowa: The First 150 Years" in 2006 to celebrate the town's sesquicentennial.
The Cambridge City Center houses the Cambridge Memorial Library, founded in 1946, and a versatile events hall used for community gatherings.
Cambridge is part of the Ames, Iowa Metropolitan Statistical Area, which is within the larger Ames‑Boone Combined Statistical Area.
